targetWords.definition: Charity is an act of giving help, usually money, to those who need it.
targetWords.example: Thanks to his friends' charity, he had enough money to pay the rent.

targetWords.definition: Commerce is the activity of buying and selling things.
targetWords.example: ■ The new shopping mall increased the commerce in that section of town.

targetWords.definition: To condemn someone means to give them a specific punishment.
targetWords.example: The judge condemned the criminal to five years in prison.

targetWords.definition: If something is cozy, then it is comfortable, warm, and relaxing.
targetWords.example: The thick blanket made the bed very cozy.

targetWords.definition: To deplete an amount of something means to use up all of it.
targetWords.example: All the driving he was doing was depleting his car's fuel supply.

targetWords.definition: An economy is the money and businesses of a country or region.
targetWords.example: The factory was good for the economy because it brought jobs to the area.

targetWords.definition: — The emperor built roads to make travel easier throughout the empire. | r goods [gudz] n.
-* Shoes, hats, dresses and purses were the goods she wanted to buy.
targetWords.example: Shoes, hats, dresses and purses were the goods she wanted to buy.

targetWords.definition: To heed something means to obey or follow it.
targetWords.example: You should heed the advice on the sign and not drive so fast.

targetWords.definition: To hitchhike means to travel by asking for rides from passing vehicles.
targetWords.example: She didn't have a car, so she hitchhiked several miles to her brother's home.

targetWords.definition: To mock someone means to tease them in a cruel way. The girls mocked Nancy because she was a new student.
If someone is neutral, then they do not help either of the two fighting sides.
targetWords.example: The girl's friend remained neutral while the couple was arguing.

targetWords.definition: To persecute means to treat someone badly.
targetWords.example: Dan felt persecuted because he was smaller than the other boys at school.

targetWords.definition: Pity is the feeling of sadness and kindness for those who are suffering.
targetWords.example: Because she had pity for the lost boy, she helped him find his parents.

targetWords.definition: To reduce something means to make it less in size or number.
targetWords.example: ■ When the store reduced its prices, people wanted to shop there.

targetWords.definition: A scribe was a person whose job was to copy written works.
targetWords.example: In Ancient Egypt, scribes recorded important events.

targetWords.definition: A temper is someone's mood or a chance that they might get angry.
targetWords.example: She has a temper. Even the slightest mistakes make her angry.

targetWords.definition: A throne is the special chair in which a ruler sits.
targetWords.example: Nobody except the king and queen sat in the thrones in the great hall.

targetWords.definition: Unity is the state of people working together for a certain purpose.
targetWords.example: The project was finished early, thanks to the unity of the workers. V ic t o r [viktar] n.

story.passage:
A great and powerful empire needed the wood from its western areas to build palaces

and homes forthe emperor and his friends. However, the empire had depleted many of the

forests. The trees were important to the western areas' economy. With no trees to sell, the

commerce in that area was reduced. Citizens could no longer purchase the goods that they

needed to survive. Their life became difficult.

A poor scribe from the area wanted to help. He hitchhiked to the capital to ask the

emperor for charity. He was invited to the palace. It was large and cozy. Tables were loaded

with food, and fires burned warmly in every fireplace.

The emperor sat up upon his throne, and the scribe stood in front of him.

"I've come to ask for help," the scribe said. "We're all very poor and hungry. You've

used up all of the forests, and now we have nothing to sell."

Then he added a warning. "If we don't receive help, I'm

afraid that the entire empire will suffer. We must

establish some unity."

Upon hearing the scribe's request, the

emperor's bad temper surfaced. He mocked

the scribe. "You think I should help," he said

and laughed. "You should just be happy

to belong to this great empire. You will get

nothing from me."

The emperor felt no pity for the citizens

of the western area. They were condemned

to starve. The scribe returned home with

nothing.

Not long after, an enemy invaded the

empire from the west. They were marching

to the capital. Because the citizens felt

persecuted by the emperor, they remained

neutral. They didn't fight the invaders but

allowed them to march freely to the capital.

The emperor was defeated. If he had

heeded the words of the scribe, then the

citizens might have been the victors. But

because he had treated them badly, they

treated him badly in return.
